mcpRiskIntro: Read these risks before you turn it on:
mcpRiskCommands: Any program on this computer that has the access token can list your hosts and run any command on them, including deleting data or shutting a server down.
mcpRiskNoAsk: Commands from MCP do not go through the AI permission modes. They run without asking you and are only recorded in the AI audit log.
mcpRiskInjection: An agent can be steered by prompt injection in web pages, files or command output into running commands you never asked for.
mcpRiskSecrets: Passwords, keys and passphrases are never sent to agents. Hosts that need one typed are refused.
mcpRiskLocal: The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Keep the token secret, make a new one if it leaks, and turn the server off when you don’t need it.
